look_here_first: This is a WOODY branching shrub with SMALL BLUE to lavender flowers (often ~10–13 mm long), rough/hairy ovate leaves with serrated/wavy edges. Do not describe its leaves as categorically smaller than autumn sage: sizes overlap (ballotiflora ~15–38 mm vs greggii ~8–48 mm in descriptions). More useful split: balloon-flower shrub sage's distinctly textured leaf faces and tiny blue-purple corollas versus S. greggii's generally smoother leaf blades with larger often ~25-mm showy corollas. Hays introduced-from-Medina specimen is NOT proof this is wild native in Hays.
project_tracker_diagnostic: woody densely branched shrub/subshrub; small ovate leaves with serrate/wavy margins; leaf surfaces hairy/rough; small blue to purple flowers; elongated flower clusters; dry rocky limestone/scrub habitat

project_inclusion.range_basis: Medina — UT Plant Resources Center records the Hays study plant as introduced from a cliff above the Medina River in Medina County. Uvalde — Harvard University Herbaria records E.J. Palmer specimen 11337 from Uvalde and additional Sabinal material. Val Verde — official Devils River/Dan A. Hughes landscape inventory and Laughlin AFB natural-resources inventory explicitly document Salvia ballotiflora in Val Verde County.

best_field_traits: small ovate leaves with serrate/wavy margins
At close range, inspect the hairy calyx/corolla tube and upper-lip hairs; Joey notes flowers around 10 mm across.
morphology_keys.flower_detail: Showy for its size but MUCH smaller than S. greggii in comparison: blue to lavender-purple bilabiate flowers about 10–13 mm; hair on upper corolla lip/calyx, which requires focused macro.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey also notes pleasant volatile compounds/aromatic character in the leaves; treat odor as a supporting cue, not a primary ID character.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite ovate leaves roughly 15–38 mm, often coarsely toothed or crenulate/wavy, hair roughness on upper and lower faces; dimensions may overlap S. greggii.
morphology_keys.comparison_to_greggii: S. greggii also woody and may have similarly small leaves, but many cultivated S. greggii have large ~25 mm corollas and comparatively smooth elliptic foliage; don't rely on leaf LENGTH alone.
morphology_keys.hays_flora_context: UT Austin Hays flora specifically lists Salvia ballotiflora as introduced from a cliff above Medina River (Medina County) to Hays collection. This is not wild in-situ Hays nativity proof; keep historical introduction separate from source-pool learner inclusion.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Salvia greggii: Both are woody. S. ballotiflora has much smaller, inconspicuous blue-purple flowers and distinctly small hairy leaves; autumn sage usually has larger showier flowers and a different compact shrub habit.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.pair: Shrubby Blue Sage versus Autumn Sage
photo_diagnostic_lesson.first: Check a mature stem leaf surface and corolla SIDE VIEW first; both plants are woody.

compare.ballotiflora: Ovate, usually 15–38 mm, serrated/wavy and rough with obvious hairs on both faces
compare.greggii: Elliptic/obovate around 8–48 mm; generally smoother, pitted microglands; SIZE OVERLAPS
compare.photo_need: macro of upper AND underside of same-maturity leaves plus ruler

compare.ballotiflora: Blue-purple small ~10–13 mm, smaller upper lip with hair detail
compare.greggii: Larger ~25 mm tubular/lipped flower, often red/pink but cultivated purple/white/orange exist
compare.photo_need: two side-view corollas with mm ruler

compare.ballotiflora: Clusters of small blue flowers with small calyces
compare.greggii: Pairs of more showy flowers in terminal racemes

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: SHRUBBY BLUE = ROUGH toothed leaf and SMALL blue flower. AUTUMN = smoother oval leaf and BIGGER showy flower.
